text: This game created a massive challenge for me in scoring it, and deciding on wether or not I should reccomend it. On its own merits, it provides large amounts of fun and entertainment, at least for a while. The issue is, however, that there are better alternatives. Look, this review will 100% grade it on it's own, however, I am under the belief that if there's a better alternative, why get the lesser? This game has a typical Just Cause-esque action story, where you bring down an evil dictator ruling over a strong island. What I find unique is the inclusion of drug cartels, and being able to rank up with them and rebels in order to get better weapons. You play as Rico Rodriguez, a dictator removal specialist, and go through many missions in order to eventually remove the dictator. I actually haven't finished the game yet, but I have almost 10 hours of gameplay, so I can speak relatively well in this department. First, the cartels are essentially a carbon copy of the police and rebels, so there isn't too much interest there, aside from a little variation in missions. To gain their trust, you capture settlements owned by the purple cartel, or government. While it's fine at first, it's extermely repetitive, as it works the exact same every single time, with absolutely no variation aside from difficulty and weaponry, and perhaps the setting. The missions are fairly interesting, if not a little dull, but can provide some entertainment. Causing mayhem in this game is possible, with stealing cars, exploding police, etc, but can get a bit dull after a while, without enough variation. Exploration of the island would be great, as there are a few landmarks and interesting locations, but it's mostly boring and all the same, jungles and small towns. Gameplay is somewhat repetitive, but still engaging, at least for a while, or short intervals. Vehicles are usually fine to use, but controls, particularly in chases and turns, are atrocious. They are usuable and fine, but sharp turns can lead to the most ridiculous swaying, and a mission failure. It's fun at times, but often annoying. The Heavy Drop system of this game is very limited, in that it only has 4 available vehicles, but they are helpful and pretty cool in their own right. Navigation is alright, but a little wary and bothersome at times. Heavy Drops and being able to be sent to bases help, though. Gunplay is terrible, and incredibly ridiculous, and yet pretty fun. It can be incredibly annoying at times, though. Some vehicles also have weapons, and usually they are pretty powerful, and tons of fun to use. Yeah, big suprise, the graphics aren't great, but it's not terrible. It looks pretty fine, and never gets too distracting, unless your used to gorgeous looking games. The entire island, though, looks like a massive jungle with a few towns and cities, so there isn't much to see, and it kind of blends altogether. (I've decided to seperate this from Style) The game sounds really good, and the music is gorgeous. It really gives a good feeling, and fits in perfectly. It sounsd great. The sound effects work well, they sound exactly as they are and have fairly good quality. Dialoge is a little iffy, but it works alright. The only issue is when a random cop yells "Stop, Citizen!" over and over, it happens surprisingly a lot. The characters are fairly generic and forgettable, with a few exceptions. Sheldon seems fairly interesting, with his generally secrative nature. Just Cause isn't a bad game by any means, but it's not perfect. It's a lot of fun to play, and enjoyable, however, there is a far surperior alternatives. Just Cause 2, for about 7 more dollars, provides much more gameplay and entertainment, and a much more polished game. For some more, buy Just Cause 3. It's a perfection of the idea, and delivers thousands of hours of potential gameplay. I would actually get the Just Cause Pack, selling both Just Cause 1 and Just Cause 2, on sale. You could grab it for about 2-5 bucks, and get 2 pretty fun games. If it isn't on sale, however, I can't recommend it. It isn't a bad game by any means, just too mediocre for the price and considering alternatives. I may change it to a reccomendation if the price for JC2/JC3 raises, or if Just Cause's price gets reduced to maximum 5 dollars. Just Cause gets a 6/10, grab it with Just Cause 2 on sale, or just get JC2/JC3 and skip it. FOOTNOTE: Guys, there is a difference between disagreeing with a review, and it being an actual terrible review. By no means do you have to agree with everything I said, but I was as real as I could be in it, not just giving 1 sentence of "it crshed for me!".

text: With everyone bashing the game for the slow updates etc, I have been having lots of fun with this game. I was/am an avid fan on KF1 and even got all the micro transactions to support the devs. Still this sequel feels like a good work in progress, having played many tripwire games in the past it's always a bit choppy to start but they usually make it up. The game in its current state just doesn't feel as solid as KF1 yet, some good improvments but some parts feel a bit lacking compared to the orginal. Pros: - Meaty feeling guns - Cool perk special skill specs - The gore diversity is good - The explosions feel very nice - Better voice acting over the original - Maps have good ambience - Some interesting new weapons - Sound track fits the game well - The new zed knockdown system is good from first impressions Cons: - The game does feel a little unbalenced but that's to be expected at this stage, besdies I only play on Co-op so it's not like it's a game breaker - Some maps feel a bit lacking their set up and currently feel a bit uncontrolable and chaotic compared to the first (with a good team that is) - Welding seems to have become a bit useless, doors do not regenerate after a round like in KF1 - Voice acting dialog is a bit too serious (apart from the classic KF1 charecters using the old voices) - The guns still lack some of the punch of KF1 guns, but only ever so slightly. Overal liking the experience, lets hope that TWI do it justice.

text: I bought this game as soon as it was available on Early Access, and plugged away at it for 200 hours. I'm giving this game a positive review, but I must say I'm very disappointed by the full release of this game. Graphics: The game looks great. It's not perfect, but the graphics, fire and particle effects are very nicely done, the gore engine is amazing and the whole game is just big beautiful bloody mess. Environments look unique, none of the official maps look alike, none of the guns look like generic wastes (aside from some of the starting weapons, which is to be expected) and overall the game looks wonderful. Sound: The guns sound wonderful. Seriously, I love the sound the shotguns and explosives make. The only weapons I can't stand the sound of are the Medic Assault Rifle, and the melee swings for most weapons. I feel like the berserker's hammer swings just don't sound meaty enough. They don't have much oomph behind them, they're not particularly crisp or even that loud. I know I could turn the sound up, but doing so would make every other weapon shatter my ear drums. The soundtrack isn't exactly my style of music, but it fits the game perfectly. The fact that I can turn lyrics on or off only makes it that much better. The voice acting for this game is a lot better than it's predecessor. The fact that there's so many new and different voices now makes the game feel so much better to me. I love Mr. Foster, but I also love Skully. All of the female voices sound pretty decent as well. The game sounds good, but I wouldn't say it's perfect. Some weapons seriously need some different sound files. Gameplay: There are a bunch of different classes, each of which do something better than others. Berserkers are tanks and can clear mobs of enemies without dropping hundreds of dollars in ammo. Commandos can lay down long ranged, accurate rapid fire support to soften up enemies. Supports can keep doors up and provide ammo to his allies, as well as heavy, close-ranged burst damage to his enemies. They all play really well, and they handle in a way that's unique. Then there's the Survivalist special snowflake. This is one of the issues with the game a lot of people seem to have. When this game was fully released, all that was added from the Early Access version was an assault rifle for the demolitions class, and the survivalist class, who has almost no special abilities at all. He just uses the weapons from all the other classes. The fact that the update that released this class took so long after the previous update where they added maps rubs a lot of people the wrong way, myself included. Also, the idea that an Early Access game that didn't even have all of its maps done yet had developers spending time, money and effort creating weapon skins for microtransactions over finishing their game's levels was a less than promising concept to me. I'd give this game a solid 8/10, especially when I consider the Steam Workshop support this game has. Just the other day a friend and I played a full recreation of Bikini Bottom where we murdered zombies in various copyright free Spongebob places It's a great game. It's a lot of fun. I just wish the developers hadn't released it the way they had.
